newsitem.title: INDIA: India seen issuing bond to tap banks' excess funds.
newsitem.headline: India seen issuing bond to tap banks' excess funds.

text.p: A fresh government bond issue to mop up excess liquidity with banks is likely in the next few days, although the government has already completed about half of the current year's budgeted borrowing.
Money market dealers said market players seemed to have already discounted a new bond issue.

"In the last couple of days, trade in securities has become a bit cautious," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The insitutions and long-term investors are still buying but traders have become wary...everyone is speculating about the new issue."
"Expectations on the new bond are varied.. some people are talking of a medium-term bond, some of a floating rate bond, some are talking of a 10- or even 15-year bond," he said.
The dealer said he expected the new stock to be either a four-year zero-coupon bond or a six-year security.
Aashish Pitale, manager debt research at ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said he expected the government to announce a four-year zero-coupon bond.

"We have a zero-coupon 1999 and a zero-coupon 2000," he said. "I think a zero 2001 will fit in nicely. It is important to have a yield curve for zero-coupon bonds along with a curve for securities at par."
"Further we have yet not had a zero-coupon bond issue this year," he said.
"The banking system is flush with funds," said Pitale.

"Call money rates have been below 4.0 percent for five days now despite substantial funds locked up with the central bank," Pitale said, referring to a July 7 repo auction where the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mopped up 45 billion rupees.

"This is an indication of the liquidity available with the system," Pitale said. "I think there must be another 50 billion rupees of surplus funds floating around and an auction at this stage will go through easily."
Pitale said the government had completed around 50 percent of its budgeted borrowings for 1997/98 (April-March).
"It has borrowed 263.98 billion rupees out of a budgeted figure of 535.68 billion, including treasury bills and a private placement of 50 billion rupees with the RBI," he said.
